references.note: Approved disc, light, camera and matte miniature finish; do not copy its creature. Match this disc's own lightness EXACTLY -- do not darken it further.

Native shape (64x128 tall body): a BARE-CHESTED male naga with a pearl set in his chest and a crested helm, holding a round shield and a heavy mace over a serpent tail. Keep the bare torso and the pearl; do NOT copy the gold breastplate of the superseded flat token.

The SUPERSEDED slasul flat token for this same identity: pose family, naga-with-mace-and-shield composition, disc and camera are correct and must be kept, but its gold breastplate covering the torso is the exact defect -- the desc requires a bare torso with the pearl visible. Remove only the chest armour; keep everything else.

prompt_fields.subject: A towering regal male naga seen from a steep overhead three-quarter angle: a muscular BARE torso -- chest and abdomen entirely uncovered, with NO breastplate, NO cuirass, NO scale-mail and NO chest armour of any kind -- carrying an exquisite large WHITE PEARL set directly in the centre of his bare chest. A bronze-gold crested helm with a tall fin-shaped crest frames his stern masculine tanned face; a gold collar and gold armbands sit on the bare shoulders and arms. A round bronze-rimmed shield with a pearl boss is held forward on the left arm and a heavy flanged mace is raised on the right. Below the waist a thick SEA-GREEN serpent tail with a pale cream belly is coiled in a broad round spiral base beneath him, gold-edged scales. Regal, bare-chested, coiled and complete.
prompt_fields.contrast: Nagas: SLASUL is the GOLD-CRESTED bare-chested naga king with a large pearl set directly in his BARE chest, a round shield forward and a mace raised, on a sea-green spiral tail base (silhouette: fin-crested helm above a round shield and a raised mace over a round coiled base; hue: sea green and bronze-gold with a white pearl; value: mid-light). This repaint reverses the superseded v1, which wrongly clad his torso in a gold breastplate; the desc says his 'torso is bare apart from an exquisite pearl set directly in his chest'. The shipped myrmidon has a blue tail and a trident, the tidewarden is brown with a shield, the nereid is yellow-tailed, zoisla red-tailed, nashva teal-tailed, the tidecaller grey robed: none of those is a bare-chested gold-helmed pearl-bearing naga king.
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Disc plate discipline: measured results show generations of this style reference tend to render the disc DARKER than the reference, never lighter. So do not darken the disc at all: render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band and the area under the creature -- at reference lightness, a hair lighter, never darker (the style reference's own brightness). No warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette anywhere on the disc. Do not darken the creature to compensate either. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures. The ENTIRE creature, every limb, tail, wing, drip, staff and effect included, fits inside a circle of about three quarters of the disc radius around the disc centre, leaving a wide bare charcoal ring of base plate on every side, yet the creature is large and bold inside that circle. Draw the creature COMPACT and chunky: limbs, weapons, tools, cloth and effects are pulled in so the whole silhouette forms one rounded mass inside the inner three quarters of the disc; no tip, blade, hat brim, tentacle end or tail reaches the outer sixth ring band or crosses the disc rim. Value discipline (measured lesson from earlier tokens): the creature's large masses are MID-LIGHT to LIGHT in value, clearly LIGHTER than the charcoal disc, with broad pale highlight planes on every upper-left surface, so the silhouette reads as a bright shape on the dark disc at very small size. Nothing near-black except tiny eye slits and thin seams; no black cloth, black leather, black armour or black fur anywhere.
prompt_fields.palette: Warm tanned BARE skin on the torso and arms in a mid-light value with broad pale highlight planes, sea-green serpent tail with pale jade highlights and a cream belly, bronze-gold fin-crested helm, collar and armbands, white pearl, pale steel mace head; NO gold or bronze breastplate and NO chest armour anywhere on the torso. Nothing darker than dark green except the eyes and seams; the disc stays neutral charcoal with no green or gold cast. Dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel, kept a visibly lighter value than the creature's darkest parts so the two never merge.

refinement.design_change_reason: The shipped flat token was generated with a gold breastplate covering the whole torso, which directly contradicts slasul's own desc: 'His torso is bare apart from an exquisite pearl set directly in his chest, and in his muscular arms he holds ready a heavy mace and shield.' The survey of 2026-10-04 flagged the breastplate as a desc conflict. This repaint keeps the naga pose family, crested helm, round shield, heavy mace, spiral sea-green tail, disc and camera, and changes only the torso to bare tanned skin with the pearl clearly set in the centre of the chest. It is a flat-token repaint only; wiring and the manifest id are unchanged.
